df = pd.read_csv("yellow_tripdata_2024-01.csv")   # runs NOW
df = df[df["fare_amount"] > 0]                      # runs NOW

caption: Every line executes the moment Python reaches it. By line 3, lines 1-2 have already fully run.

eyebrow: Spark — lazy, until you ask for a result
code:
df = spark.read.parquet("cleansed/yellow_tripdata_2024-01.parquet")
df = df.filter(df["fare_amount"] > 0)
df = df.groupBy("VendorID").count()
# Nothing has run yet. Not the read. Not the filter.

df.show()   # THIS triggers everything above, all at once
caption: Every line just adds a step to a plan — Spark doesn't touch real data until an action asks for a result.

eyebrow: Why this matters — and the common surprise
code:
df.filter(df["fare_amount"] < 0)
# ...nothing happens. No error either.
# filter() built a plan nothing ever asked to run.
caption: Because the whole plan is visible before running, Spark can optimize it — skip steps, combine passes. Pandas can't.
